reasoning: Both reviewers independently converge on the same core diagnosis: this manuscript presents specific numerical claims (20% IoU improvement, 30% processing time reduction) without any actual data, results, tables, figures, defined methodology, ground truth, or benchmark dataset. The paper reads as an incomplete template rather than a finished study. Three independently fatal gaps — missing method specification, missing results/data, and missing ground truth/evaluation basis — each individually prevent the central conclusions from being supported. These assessments survived both reviewers' reflections without downgrade. Additional major concerns (undefined baselines, absent statistical analysis, placeholder references, internal inconsistency between general pose estimation framing and trivial curl-counter content) reinforce but are secondary to the fundamental evidentiary void.

findings.finding: No specific algorithmic modifications are described. The paper claims 'novel modifications', 'refined algorithms', and 'advanced neural network architectures' but provides no architecture details, training procedure, parameter changes, loss functions, or any concrete specification of what was changed relative to standard MediaPipe.
findings.justification: If the proposed method is unspecified, the claimed improvements cannot be attributed to any defined intervention, reproduced, or scientifically evaluated. Both reviewers flagged this independently at the highest severity and neither downgraded on reflection. The paper's central conclusion — that specific enhancements improved MediaPipe — is unsupported without a described method.

findings.finding: No quantitative results are reported despite specific numerical claims. The manuscript asserts a 20% IoU improvement and 30% processing time reduction but provides no tables, figures, baseline values, per-condition numbers, variance estimates, sample sizes, or statistical tests. Referenced Table 1 and Figures 2-3 do not appear in the manuscript.
findings.justification: The central evidence for the paper's conclusions is entirely absent. Both reviewers rated this retraction-worthy and strengthened their conviction on reflection. The missing internal exhibits (Table 1, Figures 2-3) suggest the manuscript is incomplete or assembled from a template. Without any underlying data, the headline claims have zero evidentiary support.

findings.finding: No dataset or ground truth is defined for pose estimation evaluation. The paper mentions recording walking/running videos but does not identify any benchmark dataset (COCO, MPII, Human3.6M), describe a custom dataset's size/diversity/annotation protocol, or explain how true joint locations were obtained for computing accuracy metrics.
findings.justification: Pose estimation accuracy cannot be validly quantified without ground-truth pose annotations. If no ground truth exists, reported MSE and IoU values are uninterpretable. Both reviewers flagged this at the highest severity and maintained it through reflection. This independently invalidates the accuracy claims.

findings.finding: The accuracy metrics (MSE, IoU) are undefined or mismatched for landmark-based pose estimation. MSE is given without defining what Y represents, and IoU is introduced without specifying what regions are being overlapped for a landmark model. Standard pose estimation metrics (PCK, OKS/mAP, MPJPE) are not used.
findings.justification: Reviewer A initially rated this retraction-worthy but downgraded to major-revision on reflection, noting that landmark tasks can sometimes be evaluated via derived regions. Reviewer B identified this as a missed finding and suggested retraction-worthy. Given the ambiguity — the metrics could potentially be defined validly but simply aren't explained — major-revision is appropriate. The undefined metrics seriously undermine but do not definitively invalidate the claims, especially since no actual metric values are reported anyway.

findings.finding: Internal inconsistency between general pose estimation framing and trivial curl-counter content. The paper frames itself as optimizing human pose estimation broadly, but the only concrete algorithmic content is an elbow-angle threshold for counting bicep curls.
findings.justification: Both reviewers identified this scope mismatch. The title and conclusions claim broad pose estimation advances, but the experiments (to the extent anything is described) concern only a narrow exercise-counting application. This creates material ambiguity about what was actually studied and could make the paper misleading, but it is potentially repairable with proper scoping.

findings.finding: No baseline comparison is properly defined. The paper claims benchmarking against 'traditional models' and a 'baseline MediaPipe model' but does not specify software version, hardware, inference settings, confidence thresholds, image resolution, model complexity, or which specific comparator models were used.
findings.justification: Both reviewers flagged this. Performance comparisons in real-time vision are highly configuration-sensitive. Without a defined baseline, the claimed improvements are uninterpretable. This is a serious but potentially correctable reporting failure.

findings.finding: No statistical analysis is presented despite claims of 'advanced statistical methods.' There are no hypothesis tests, uncertainty estimates, repeated-run summaries, or evidence that observed differences exceed normal variation.
findings.justification: Reviewer A flagged this at major-revision, and Reviewer B noted it reinforces the retraction-worthy severity of missing results. As a standalone issue, the absence of statistics means claimed improvements cannot be distinguished from noise, but this is correctable. The finding is largely moot given no results exist to analyze.

findings.finding: Data collection is inadequately specified: no number of subjects, demographic composition, camera setup, frame rate, resolution, recording protocol, train/validation/test split, or inclusion/exclusion criteria are reported.
findings.justification: Reviewer A flagged this; Reviewer B's dataset finding overlaps. These omissions prevent assessment of bias, overfitting, and external validity. Correctable with proper reporting.

findings.finding: Claims of improved performance under occlusion and low light lack any controlled evaluation protocol for these conditions.
findings.justification: Reviewer A flagged this. Robustness claims require condition-specific experiments. Without them, these conclusions are unsubstantiated. Correctable with proper experimental design.

findings.finding: Unsupported broad claims such as 'sets a new benchmark' and 'substantially advanced the state of the art' without any state-of-the-art benchmark comparison.

findings.finding: No details on hardware, software environment, or reproducibility (CPU/GPU type, frame resolution, frame rate, OS) for benchmarking.
findings.justification: Reviewer B flagged this as minor. Important for reproducibility but secondary given the more fundamental absences. Would not change conclusions on its own.

findings.finding: The GitHub repository link is provided but the manuscript does not tie its claims to specific scripts, configurations, or commits in the repository.
findings.justification: Both reviewers rated this as minor. Code availability does not compensate for missing methods/results in the manuscript itself.

findings.justification: Reviewer A flagged this. Weakens user-experience claims but does not determine validity of technical conclusions.

review_a.reasoning: The manuscript, as presented, lacks the methodological details and results required to support its central claims of improved MediaPipe pose estimation accuracy and efficiency. The paper appears internally inconsistent about the task being studied (general pose estimation benchmark vs. a simple curl-counter angle heuristic), provides no reproducible description of the proposed algorithmic modifications, omits essential dataset/ground-truth information, and reports headline performance gains without underlying numerical evidence, statistical analysis, or valid benchmarking details. These issues are serious enough that the main conclusions cannot be verified from the data and methods presented.

findings.finding: The central methodological contribution is not actually described. The paper repeatedly claims 'novel modifications', 'refined algorithms', and 'advanced neural network architectures' added to MediaPipe, but gives no concrete architecture, training procedure, parameter changes, optimization method, loss function, implementation details, or ablation.
findings.justification: If the proposed method is unspecified, the claimed improvements cannot be attributed to any defined intervention, reproduced, or scientifically evaluated. The paper's central conclusion—that specific enhancements improved MediaPipe—cannot be supported as presented.

findings.finding: No usable experimental results are reported. The manuscript references Table 1 and Figures 2 and 3, and claims a 20% IoU improvement and 30% processing-time reduction, but provides no actual table contents, baseline values, variance estimates, sample sizes, confidence intervals, or per-condition numbers.
findings.justification: Without the underlying results, there is no evidentiary basis for the headline claims. If confirmed, the central conclusions about improved accuracy and efficiency are unsupported by the presented data.

findings.finding: The evaluation design lacks any defined ground truth or benchmark dataset for pose estimation accuracy. The paper mentions recording walking/running videos but does not state how true joint locations were obtained, what annotations exist, or how prediction error was measured against reference labels.
findings.justification: Pose estimation accuracy cannot be validly quantified without ground-truth poses or a recognized benchmark. If no ground truth exists, metrics like MSE and IoU are uninterpretable, invalidating the core accuracy claims.

findings.finding: The selected accuracy metrics are methodologically mismatched or undefined for the stated task. MSE is given as (Yi - Yhat_i)^2 without defining what Y represents in pose estimation, and IoU is introduced without specifying what regions/bounding entities are being overlapped for a landmark-based pose model.
findings.justification: For landmark pose estimation, standard metrics would typically be PCK, OKS/mAP, MPJPE, or landmark error. Using undefined or task-inappropriate metrics means the reported 'accuracy improvement' may not measure pose estimation quality at all. That would fundamentally break the main inference.

findings.finding: The manuscript is internally inconsistent about the actual study objective: it frames the work as general human pose estimation optimization, but the only concrete algorithmic content concerns elbow-angle calculation and a rule-based curl counter.
findings.justification: This creates substantial ambiguity about what was evaluated: a full pose-estimation model, a downstream exercise-classification heuristic, or both. Conclusions about broad pose-estimation advances may be overstated if the experiments only concern a narrow curl-counter application.

findings.finding: No baseline comparison is properly defined. The paper claims benchmarking against 'traditional models' and a 'baseline MediaPipe model' but does not specify software version, hardware, inference settings, confidence thresholds, image resolution, model complexity, or which comparator models were used.
findings.justification: Performance and latency comparisons in real-time vision are highly sensitive to configuration. Poorly specified baselines can materially change conclusions, though the issue might be repairable with full reporting.

findings.finding: No statistical analysis is actually presented despite claims of 'advanced statistical methods.' There are no hypothesis tests, uncertainty estimates, repeated-run summaries, or evidence that observed differences exceed normal variation.
findings.justification: Without uncertainty quantification, it is unclear whether the claimed improvements are robust or due to noise, hardware fluctuation, or sampling variation. This could change conclusions but does not by itself prove them false.

findings.finding: Data collection is inadequately specified: no number of subjects, demographic composition, camera setup, frame rate, resolution, recording protocol, train/validation/test split, or inclusion/exclusion criteria are reported.
findings.justification: These omissions prevent assessment of bias, overfitting, and external validity. They could materially affect conclusions about robustness and general applicability.

findings.finding: The manuscript claims improved performance under occlusion and low light, but no controlled evaluation protocol for these conditions is described.
findings.justification: Claims about robustness to specific environmental factors require condition-specific experiments. Without them, those conclusions are unsubstantiated and may change under proper testing.

findings.finding: There is no evidence that the comparisons avoid data leakage or tuning on the evaluation set. The paper does not describe how optimization decisions were separated from final assessment.
findings.justification: If model refinements were tuned on the same scenarios used for evaluation, reported gains may be inflated. This is a serious but potentially correctable methodological concern.

findings.finding: The use of participant/operator feedback as part of the evaluation is described, but no instrument, scale, sample size, or analysis method is provided.
findings.justification: This weakens any user-experience claims, but it does not by itself determine the validity of the technical conclusions.

findings.finding: The reference list and citations contain multiple placeholders, likely fabricated/generic entries, and incomplete bibliographic information ([JOURNAL], generic author names such as 'Developer, B.' and 'Researcher, A.').
findings.justification: This raises credibility concerns about the literature foundation and may indicate poor scholarship or non-verifiable sourcing. While not by itself invalidating the empirical results, it is a substantial concern requiring correction.

findings.finding: The paper repeatedly uses broad claims such as 'sets a new benchmark' and 'substantially advanced the state of the art' without any state-of-the-art benchmark protocol or comparison to established datasets.
findings.justification: These claims are not methodologically justified and could mislead readers about the scope of the evidence. They should be removed or supported by proper benchmarking.

findings.finding: The code availability statement does not compensate for missing methods/results in the manuscript; no specific commit, release, or mapping from code to experiments is provided.
findings.justification: This limits reproducibility but is secondary to the more fundamental absence of methodological and evaluative detail in the paper itself.

review_b.reasoning: The manuscript fails to provide any actual data, results, or reproducible methodology. It reads as a generic, unsubstantiated template rather than a completed study. Claims of '20% improvement in IoU' and '30% reduction in processing time' are presented without any experimental data, tables, figures, or statistical evidence. The paper lacks a clearly defined dataset, baseline comparison methodology, and specific algorithmic modifications. These omissions render the central conclusions unsupported by any verifiable data.

findings.finding: No quantitative results reported despite specific numerical claims. The manuscript states '20% increase in IoU' and '30% reduction in processing time' but provides no table, figure, or statistical test showing these results. No confidence intervals, no sample sizes, no comparison to baselines are given.
findings.justification: The central claims of the paper (improved accuracy and efficiency) are presented as concrete numbers but with zero supporting data. This is a fundamental reporting failure—if the numbers exist, they are not presented; if they do not exist, the claims are fabricated. Either way, the conclusions cannot be supported.

findings.finding: No dataset description or source. The paper mentions 'high-resolution cameras' and 'systematic recording of human activities' but does not identify any standard benchmark dataset (e.g., COCO, MPII, Human3.6M) or describe a custom dataset in terms of size, diversity, annotation protocol, or evaluation split.
findings.justification: Without knowing what data was used, no independent verification or replication is possible. The entire experimental basis is absent. This invalidates any reported performance figures.

findings.finding: No specific algorithmic modifications are described. The paper refers to 'refined algorithms' and 'advanced neural network architectures' but provides no equations, network diagrams, layer descriptions, loss functions, or training details that distinguish the proposed method from standard MediaPipe.
findings.justification: A methodology section that fails to specify what was actually changed means the study cannot be evaluated, reproduced, or even understood. The claimed enhancements are effectively unspecified, so no conclusion about their efficacy can be drawn.

findings.finding: Section 4 (Results) contains no actual results. It presents equations (MSE, IoU) that are not used with any data, refers to 'Table 1' and 'Figure 2' and 'Figure 3' which do not appear in the manuscript, and gives vague qualitative statements like 'significant enhancements'.
findings.justification: The results section is entirely empty of data. The paper's conclusions rest on figures and tables that are not provided. This is a fatal omission—the central evidence for the claims is missing.

findings.finding: The curl counter logic (Eq for stage determination) is presented as a key contribution but is trivial arithmetic (angle thresholding). No validation of its accuracy, no comparison to ground truth, and no integration with the claimed 'optimizations' is shown.
findings.justification: If this is considered part of the contribution, it needs experimental validation. As presented, it is a simple thresholding exercise with no evidence it works. However, it may be incidental to the main claim, hence not retraction-worthy alone.

findings.finding: References are incomplete or improperly formatted. Several references have placeholder '[JOURNAL]' or '[JOURNAL]/CVF', and some authors (e.g., 'Developer, B.', 'Innovator, C.', 'Researcher, A.') appear fabricated or are generic placeholders.
findings.justification: If these references do not exist, the literature review is partially fabricated, which undermines the scholarly integrity. If they are real but misformatted, this is sloppy but fixable. Either way, the paper's scholarly foundation is questionable.

findings.finding: The paper lacks a clear statement of the baseline model used for comparison. It claims 'compared to existing solutions' but does not specify which version of MediaPipe (e.g., BlazePose, PoseLandmarker) or other models (e.g., OpenPose) were used as the comparator.
findings.justification: Without a defined baseline, the claimed improvements are meaningless. The reader cannot interpret the 20% IoU increase because it is unclear whether the comparison is against standard MediaPipe, a prior version, or some other method.

findings.finding: No details on hardware, software environment, or reproducibility. The paper does not mention CPU/GPU type, frame resolution, frame rate, or operating system used for benchmarking.
findings.justification: This is a common omission but important for reproducibility. Given the other fatal flaws, this is a secondary concern. However, in isolation, it would require a minor revision to add.

findings.finding: The GitHub repository link (https://github.com/avhixd/Human_pose_estimation) is not reviewed, but the manuscript itself provides no evidence that the repository contains the actual code used. The paper does not reference specific scripts or configurations.
findings.justification: Even if the repo exists, the manuscript does not tie its claims to the code. This is a common but minor omission. However, if the repo is empty or unrelated, this would become a major issue.

reflection_a.reflection_notes: On second pass, I still think the manuscript has multiple fatal support gaps, but I would narrow RETRACTION-WORTHY to findings that directly make the headline conclusions unverifiable from the paper as presented. Some of my earlier ratings were probably too aggressive where the issue is serious ambiguity or poor reporting rather than a demonstrated invalidation. In particular, the missing method, missing results, and missing ground-truth/evaluation basis remain fatal. By contrast, metric mismatch/undefined IoU is very serious, but because landmark tasks can sometimes be evaluated via derived regions or auxiliary tasks, I should rate that as MAJOR-REVISION unless the paper explicitly uses those metrics incorrectly. Likewise, the lack of statistical analysis, data-collection detail, occlusion/low-light protocol, and possible leakage are important but not by themselves retraction-level. I also continue to think the paper looks like an incomplete/template manuscript, which strengthens the concern that the central claims are unsupported, but severity should track epistemic consequence rather than frustration with quality.

reflection_b.reflection_notes: Upon re-examination, I find that my original severity ratings were generally appropriate but I may have been slightly conservative on findings relating to the missing results section and the lack of dataset description. The other reviewer's analysis reinforces that these are indeed central to the paper's validity. I also notice I may have over-rated the 'GitHub repository' finding as MINOR when it should be MAJOR-REVISION given the paper's reliance on code for reproducibility, but the manuscript's own failure to tie claims to code is already covered by other findings. The 'curl counter logic' finding could arguably be upgraded to RETRACTION-WORTHY if it is the only concrete contribution, but since it is incidental to the main claim, MAJOR-REVISION remains appropriate. The 'hardware details' finding is correctly MINOR. Overall, my assessment is largely consistent with the other reviewer's high-confidence flagged verdict.
